label: Seed cohort, v1, assembled from published industry sources. Sample sizes and definitions vary by source. Marga Consortium panel data replaces this from wave one.
$readThisFirst: Every figure below traces to a citation in `sources`, and nothing here was estimated, modeled, or filled in to make a screen look complete. That has one large consequence, stated plainly in `limitations.noDistributions`: the published sources report MEANS, not distributions. A percentile requires a distribution. So no metric in this cohort can yield a percentile, and the calculator returns a ratio to the published average instead, labeled as such. Inventing a spread around a published mean would be exactly the false precision this file exists to avoid.

limitations.noDistributions: No source below publishes a percentile distribution for any practice-level metric. Every entry is therefore `central` only, with `distribution: null`. The calculator's percentile path is built and tested against fixtures, and activates without code change when Consortium wave one supplies real distributions.
limitations.noPracticeLevelOperations: Nothing published covers treatment rooms per location, injector FTEs, open hours, retail attach, membership penetration, or marketing spend at practice level. Those metrics are listed in `unavailable` with the reason. The calculator computes the user's own figure and shows the plain-language read, with no comparison attached.
limitations.noGeographicCuts: No published source breaks practice economics by state or metro tier. Those cuts are declared unavailable so the interface does not offer a comparison it cannot make.
limitations.selfReported: AmSpa figures are self-reported survey responses from member and non-member medical spas. Respondents skew toward practices engaged enough with the industry to answer a survey.
limitations.knownInconsistency: AmSpa reports mean annual revenue of $1,398,833, mean visits of 245 per month, and mean spend of $527 per visit. Those do not reconcile: 245 x 12 x $527 is $1,549,380, about 10.8 percent higher. They are means of different subsamples of the same survey and are not expected to multiply out. Both are recorded as published rather than silently adjusted.

sources.title: 2024 Medical Spa State of the Industry Executive Report
sources.method: Self-reported industry survey. The public recap does not state the respondent count, so cohort n is unknown rather than assumed.
sources.access: Public recap page. The full executive report is a paid AmSpa product and was not used.

sources.title: 2024 ASPS Procedural Statistics Report
sources.method: National procedure volume reported by ASPS member and surveyed non-member physicians.
sources.caveat: National PROCEDURE counts, not practice-level economics. A ratio derived from them describes the national procedure mix and is not a distribution of practice mixes.

sources.title: ASDS Survey on Dermatologic Procedures
sources.reason: Named in the brief as a source. No figure from it is used in v1, because none was read and verified. Listing it here without a figure attached is deliberate: it records the intent without implying a citation that does not exist.

sources.title: Public MSO and manufacturer filings and transcripts
sources.reason: Public aesthetics issuers are manufacturers (InMode, Cutera, Evolus, Revance) rather than practice operators, so their filings report device and injectable sell-through, not practice unit economics. No pure-play medical spa operator of scale files publicly. Nothing usable for a practice benchmark was found.

all.label: All medical spas
all.nBasis: Unknown. The public AmSpa recap does not state a respondent count. Treated as under 30 by the interface, which widens every band and shows the caveat rather than implying precision.

annual_revenue.quote: average annual medical spa revenue increased to $1,398,833 in 2024, from $1,307,587 in 2023

average_ticket.quote: Patients spend an average of $527 during a medical spa visit

returning_patient_share.quote: 73% of medical spa patients are repeat patients

employees_per_location.note: Single-location practices. Multi-location practices average 12 at their primary location. This is total staff, not injector FTEs, and must not be read as an injector count.

filler_to_toxin_ratio.unit: HA filler procedures per neuromodulator procedure
filler_to_toxin_ratio.derivation: 5,331,426 hyaluronic acid filler procedures divided by 9,883,711 neuromodulator procedures, both ASPS 2024.
filler_to_toxin_ratio.note: A national procedure-volume ratio, not a practice-level distribution. It answers what the country did, not what a typical practice does, and a practice differing from it is not thereby unusual.

unavailable.revenue_per_injector_chair_hour: No published source reports injector FTEs or open hours at practice level, so there is no denominator to build a benchmark from. The calculator computes the practice's own figure and explains it, with no comparison.
unavailable.revenue_per_treatment_room: No published source reports treatment rooms per location.
unavailable.retail_attach_rate: No published source separates retail from service revenue at practice level.
unavailable.membership_penetration: No published source reports membership counts against active patient counts.
unavailable.new_patient_acquisition_cost: No published source reports practice marketing spend.
unavailable.revenue_per_new_patient: Derivable only from a new-patient count, which no source reports. AmSpa reports repeat patient SHARE against visits, which is a different denominator and cannot be substituted.

unavailableCuts.state: No published source breaks practice economics by state.
unavailableCuts.metro_tier: No published source breaks practice economics by metro density.
